data.long_meaning: Amolraj is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Amol' meaning 'Immortal' and 'Raj' meaning 'Ruler'. In Hindu mythology, Amolraj is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is the preserver of the universe. The name Amolraj carries the meaning “Immortal Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amolraj usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In Hindu culture, the name Amolraj is associated with the unwavering power and immortality of Lord Vishnu, who is widely revered and worshipped as a god of preservation and sustainability. The person with this name is believed to possess a strong, spiritual foundation and an unwavering sense of purpose.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Amolraj' is derived from the Sanskrit language and consists of two parts: 'Amol' meaning 'immeasurable' and 'Raj' meaning 'king'. This name is a beautiful combination of power, strength, and immeasurability, making it a perfect choice for a baby boy.

historical_references.reference: Amolraj was a Jain monk and scholar from the 12th century CE who is known for his commentary on the 'Agama' scriptures. He wrote the 'Amolakalpa-sravakabhasya', which is a comprehensive commentary on the 'Agama' literature. His work is considered an important contribution to Jain scholarship.

Amolraj is also mentioned in the 'Sriharshacharita' of Nayaka king Sarfoji II, who ruled Thanjavur in the 18th century CE. The text describes Amolraj as a great scholar and a teacher of Sarfoji's son, Maratha king Serfoji I. Amolraj is said to have influenced the king's patronage of the arts and literature.
